name: Higgs inflation runs at xi ~ 1.7e4 (Bezrukov-Shaposhnikov)

source.located: F. Bezrukov, M. Shaposhnikov, 'The Standard Model Higgs boson as the inflaton', arXiv:0710.3755v2 [hep-th] 9 Jan 2008, Phys. Lett. B659 (2008) 703; eqs (1)-(16), footnote 1, sec. 2 p.2-3, sec. 3
source.via: alphaXiv get_paper_content(fullText=true): whole letter read, 5 pp incl. references. Barcelo-Visser gr-qc/0003025v2 sec 2.1-2.3 and p.16 also READ (answer_pdf_queries) for the sign-convention comparison.

published_statement: Eq (13), p.3: 'Inserting (12) into the COBE normalization U/eps = (0.027 M_P)^4 we find the required value for xi: xi ~ sqrt(lambda/3) N_COBE/0.027^2 ~ 49000 sqrt(lambda) = 49000 m_H/(sqrt2 v).' with N_COBE ~ 62, h_COBE ~ 9.4 M_P/sqrt(xi); n ~ 1 - 8(4N+9)/(4N+3)^2 ~ 0.97 and r ~ 192/(4N+3)^2 ~ 0.0033 at N = 60. THE LETTER PRINTS NO NUMERICAL VALUE OF xi: it gives xi as a function of lambda (equivalently m_H), and in 2007 m_H was unknown (p.2: 'm_H must be below 285 GeV [21] or even 200 GeV [22]'). Conclusions p.4: 'the amplitude of scalar perturbations is proportional to the square of the Higgs mass (at fixed xi)'.
published_hypotheses: H1 action (2): S_J = int sqrt(-g){ -(M^2 + xi h^2) R/2 + (dh)^2/2 - lambda/4 (h^2 - v^2)^2 }, unitary gauge H = h/sqrt2, 'neglect all gauge interactions for the time being' (sec 2)
H2 SIGN CONVENTION, footnote 1: 'In our notations the conformal coupling is xi = -1/6'; the effective Planck coefficient is M^2 + xi h^2, so xi > 0 STRENGTHENS gravity at large h
H3 regime 1 << sqrt(xi) << 1e17, 'in which M ~ M_P with very good accuracy' (sec 2)
H4 slow roll, leading order in h^2 >> M_P^2/xi >> v^2 (eqs 9-12); N from (12) with the log term dropped
H5 COBE normalisation U/eps = (0.027 M_P)^4 and N_COBE ~ 62 (from T_reh ~ 2e15 GeV, g* = 106.75)

H6 lambda in (13) is the tree-level relation lambda = m_H^2/(2 v^2): no running of lambda from the electroweak to the inflationary scale enters (13); sec 3 argues radiative corrections do not spoil flatness and says of itself 'the arguments we present below are not rigorous'
H7 xi itself runs, eq (16): 'xi(M_P) ~ 2 xi(M_W)', 'delta xi/xi ~ 0.2' over the inflationary region
H8 data then: WMAP-3 (Spergel 2007) for (n_s, r); m_H unknown
hypothesis_drift: ADDED DATUM -- higgs.py:213 'XI_HIGGS_INFLATION = 1.7e4 # Bezrukov-Shaposhnikov' and higgs.py:150 'Higgs inflation runs at xi ~ 1.7e4 (Bezrukov-Shaposhnikov...)': the source prints no number; 1.7e4 is eq (13) evaluated with m_H ~ 125 GeV (measured 2012, after the paper) at tree-level lambda. Computed here: 49000 x 125.13/(sqrt2 x 246.22) = 17,608, so '1.7e4' is a truncation of 1.76e4 (1.8e4 to two figures). Not an error; an attribution of a later evaluation to the paper.

DROPPED H6 (tree-level lambda) -- higgs.py:150-151, :213, :477-482; xigate.py:28-47, :141, :191-196, :269-275: xi is treated as a fixed constant of Higgs inflation, but (13) makes xi proportional to sqrt(lambda) at the inflationary scale. With SM running and the measured top mass (172.6 GeV, captures/PDG-2026.tsv pdgid 6) lambda there is small or negative; READ later values: xi ~ 1500 (Rubio 1807.02376 Fig. 6), ~800 and down to ~500 (Masina-Quiros 2412.03284 Fig. 2-3), O(10) at the critical point (Rubio sec 3.3).

DROPPED H2 (sign convention) -- higgs.py:150-151, :471-482, :634-639 and xigate.py:28-47, :191-196 place Higgs inflation's xi on Barcelo-Visser's xi > 0 axis. BV (gr-qc/0003025, READ) use conformal xi = +1/6 and effective coefficient kappa - xi phi^2 (eqs 2.1, 2.3); B-S use conformal xi = -1/6 and M^2 + xi h^2 (eq 2, footnote 1); same field normalisation (B-S H = h/sqrt2, BV (1/2) xi R phi^2). Hence xi_BV = -xi_BS (sympy, check E). In BV's convention Higgs inflation has xi ~ -1.7e4, which is BV sec 2.3 CASE 1: 'If xi < 0 ... ANEC is satisfied' -- kappa - xi phi^2 has no zero at any field value. This STRENGTHENS higgs.py's refusal (the Higgs-inflation coupling is not merely 28 orders short, it is on the branch with no gate); it UNDERMINES xigate.py's framing 'a coupling already in use' (xigate.py:34-36), which compares a BV-convention requirement of +1.48e4 with a coupling that is -1.7e4 in BV's convention. Recorded, not repaired.

DROPPED H7 (scale of xi) -- higgs.py:477-482 compares the inflation-scale xi with a gate evaluated at the electroweak VEV; by the paper's own eq (16) text xi(M_W) ~ xi(M_P)/2 ~ 8.8e3; moves 'orders short' from 27.76 to 28.05. Does not move the conclusion.

DROPPED H3/H4/H5 -- the tree carries none of the regime, slow-roll-order or normalisation hypotheses; each moves xi by a few per cent only (N* 55-62 and both normalisations give 1.6e4-2.0e4 at tree lambda, check C).
STATUS -- higgs.py:150, :213 and xigate.py:41, :141 mark the source NAMED-NOT-READ; it is now READ.

OWNERS -- the canonical entry lists only higgs.py; xigate.py:141 imports the constant and pins 'the GUT requirement is 0.872x Higgs inflation's' (xigate.py:272-275), a comparison that holds only at tree-level lambda (check D).
The canonical hypothesis 'Higgs inflation with CMB-normalised amplitude (not stated)' is faithful to H5 as far as it goes.

rederivation.outcome: ALL CHECKS PASS (exit 0). A: the large-xi Einstein-frame reduction reproduced exactly -- dchi/dx = sqrt6 M/(2(1+x)), eps = 4/(3x^2) exactly, eta = 4(1-x)/(3x^2) (paper's (10) is its large-x term), zeta^2 -> 16/(9x^2), dN/dx = 3x/(4(1+x)), h_end = 1.0746 M/sqrt(xi); eq (13) xi = sqrt(lambda/3) N/0.027^2 derived symbolically, coefficient 49,102.5 at N=62. Two presentational discrepancies, neither an error: h_COBE ~ 9.4 matches the EXACT N(x) (9.356), not the leading (12) the text cites (9.155); n = 1 - 8(4N+9)/(4N+3)^2 needs the EXACT eta, not the printed leading (10) (which gives 8(4N+12); n(60) 0.96627 vs 0.96586, both '0.97'). B: at the tree's READ m_H = 125.13 GeV, xi = 17,608 -> the tree's 1.7e4 is a truncation of 1.76e4. C: current normalisation and N* = 55-62: 1.70e4-1.91e4 at tree lambda; Rubio's 800 N sqrt(lambda) reproduced as the leading form at his A_s. D: xi_required = 9.7829e31 reproduced; orders short 27.76 (pin), 28.05 (xi at M_W), 28.81 (xi 1500), 29.09 (800), 29.29 (500), 30.99 (10) -- all > 27; xigate's GUT/xi = 0.872 only at the pin, 1.68 .. 1480 otherwise. E: xi_BV = -xi_BS proved from the two papers' conformal values; at xi_BV = -1.7e4 kappa - xi phi^2 has no real zero (BV case 1).

later_literature.what: xi ~ 800 N* sqrt(lambda) = 47200 sqrt(lambda) at N* ~ 59 (2.40, 2.42) with Planck normalisation; lambda must be taken at the inflationary scale; three RG regimes: universal (tree predictions), critical (lambda_0 ~ 1e-6, xi ~ O(10)), hilltop; vacuum metastability can be accommodated only through unknown threshold corrections (sec 3.4, Fig. 6 with xi = 1500); unitarity cutoff debate (sec 3.1).

later_literature.ref: I. Masina, M. Quiros, 'On electroweak metastability and Higgs inflation', arXiv:2412.03284 (TOP2024 proc.; based on 2403.02461, EPJC 84 (2024) 1153)
later_literature.what: for central m_t, alpha_s, m_H the SM potential is metastable (m_t^c ~ 171.0588 GeV); Higgs inflation still viable if xi flattens the potential below the barrier, with xi ~ 800 and down to ~500 near metastability; xi decreases as m_t increases.

not later literature on Higgs inflation but the other side of the tree's comparison: conformal xi = +1/6, coefficient kappa - xi phi^2 (opposite sign to B-S); case 1 'xi < 0 ... ANEC is satisfied'. Establishes xi_BV = -xi_BS.

lacked_data: The authors lacked m_H (discovered 2012), a precise m_t and NNLO/3-loop SM running (which put lambda near zero or negative at high scale -- metastability), and the Planck/ACT CMB data. EVIDENCE THAT HAVING THEM MATTERS: the number the tree attributes to them, 1.7e4, exists ONLY because of later data -- the letter gives xi as 49000 sqrt(lambda) and cannot fix it without m_H; and once lambda is run to the inflationary scale with the measured m_t, xi is no longer 1.7e4 but anywhere from ~10 (critical) to ~1.8e4 (universal, tree lambda), with ~500-1500 in the READ metastable-regime analyses -- three orders, and contested. EVIDENCE THAT IT DOES NOT MATTER for the tree's use: every value in that range leaves the Higgs 27.7-31.0 orders short of the Barcelo-Visser gate at the VEV, so higgs.py's 'more than 1e27' conclusion is untouched, and every revision LOWERS xi, i.e. widens the gap; moreover, in Barcelo-Visser's sign convention the Higgs-inflation coupling is negative and there is no gate at all. The paper's own derivation, given its inputs, re-derives exactly. The newer data do move one derived claim in the tree: xigate.py's 'the GUT-scale requirement is 0.872x the xi Higgs inflation already uses' holds only at tree-level lambda (and compares opposite-sign couplings).
grade_evidence: Source READ; eq (13) and the slow-roll chain re-derived in sympy (exit 0); at the tree's READ m_H the formula gives 17,608, so the tree's 1.7e4 is the published formula correctly evaluated (truncated). Not STANDS because the tree uses it on a wider class than the source supports: (i) the source prints a function xi = 49000 sqrt(lambda), not a number, and the number requires the tree-level-lambda hypothesis (H6) the tree drops -- with running lambda and the measured top mass, READ later work gives xi ~ 10 to ~1500; (ii) the tree drops the sign convention (H2): xi_BS = -xi_BV, so on Barcelo-Visser's axis Higgs inflation sits at xi ~ -1.7e4 (BV case 1, ANEC satisfied), not at +1.7e4. Not WRONG: nothing in the source is contradicted. Not DATA-DEPENDENT for the canonical rests_on_it: higgs.py's '28 orders short / more than 1e27' holds for every moved datum (27.7-31.0 orders; the sign drift only strengthens it). The one derived claim that IS data-dependent is xigate.py's 0.872x ratio (not in the canonical rests_on_it), recorded here, not repaired.
what_would_change_the_grade: STANDS if the tree stated the hypotheses it drops (tree-level lambda / universal regime; B-S sign convention, i.e. xi_BV ~ -1.7e4) and cited 1.7e4 as eq (13) evaluated at m_H = 125.13 GeV rather than as a number the paper prints. DATA-DEPENDENT for the canonical use only if some datum could push xi above ~1e5 (none in the literature READ here; every revision lowers xi). WRONG would need a computed contradiction of eq (13) under its own hypotheses -- none found. The ACT n_s tension (abstracts only) would be read before it is quoted either way.
